sent_to_model:
Need help with a written statement. A mom put in a complaint on me with the transportation office after I took her kindergartner back to school instead of letting her off at the stop because no adult was there. She says I "took" her daughter and wont answer her when she waved. Darlene my supervisor says I have to write my side up formal and it goes in the file AND they send a copy to the parent, so it has to be addressed to her really, Mrs. Okafor. I dont want to make it worse with her I still drive that kid every day. But I did what the policy says and I want that on paper. 28 years no write ups. Can you put it together proper, I'm not good at this kind of thing. What I want to ask is below, and please ask them to pull the camera footage too.

- Tuesday October 27, afternoon run, Bus 41, Route 9 elementary. stop is Kessler Ave and Brandt St
- student is Amara Okafor, kindergarten, Fairmont Elementary. she has the green tag on her bag = adult has to be at stop
- got to stop at 3:52, schedule says 3:50. waited till about 3:55, nobody I could see at the corner
- district rule for K riders, no adult at stop, student stays on bus and goes back to school, office calls parent
- radioed dispatch at 3:56, Gloria at dispatch called the school. Had 3 more stops and 14 kids still on
- got Amara back to Fairmont at 4:31, walked her in to Mrs. Petrakis in the office myself
- mom says she was parked across Brandt by the laundromat and waved. I did not see her. there was a box truck parked on that side
- complaint dated Oct 29, Darlene gave it to me Nov 3. statement due by Friday Nov 13
- Amara was fine, she was coloring on her folder, asked if she could ride more. I told her we were going on a little extra trip
- mom told the office I "drove off laughing". I was not laughing. I was telling the 4th grader in seat 2 to sit back down while we pulled out
- this happened once before on my route years back with a different family and they thanked me after
- I understand she was scared, I have grandkids, I would be too
- not going to say sorry for following the rule but I am sorry she had a bad afternoon
- the camera on the bus will show the stop, they should pull it
- I cant hop off and go look across the road, leaving 14 kids on a bus is not happening
- be respectful to her, no blaming, but clear that I did what I'm supposed to
- ask that she stand on the bus side of the street or step out of the car so I can see her
- say I'm glad to keep driving Amara and want this fixed
- formal, its going in my record

(About me: school bus driver, 62, Dayton, Ohio. Length: it should come to roughly 800-2,000 words.)

must_cover: Addresses Mrs. Okafor and explains the stop timeline and adherence to kindergarten release policy.
Responds to the waving and laughing claims using the supplied observations.
Acknowledges the parent’s worry, expresses regret for her difficult afternoon without apologizing for following the release policy, and requests camera footage review.
Asks Mrs. Okafor to stand on the bus side or exit her car for visibility at afternoon drop-off; affirms willingness to keep driving Amara and resolve the issue.

reference.kind: a model-written solution, used only to show the checks can be met

outputs.reason: length, assistant talk or a placeholder
